national_news.title: UDISE+ 2025-26 Report Released by Ministry of Education
bullets: The Unified District Information System for Education Plus (UDISE+) 2025-26 report covers 14.67 lakh schools, 1.03 crore teachers, and 24.72 crore students.
Maintains a favourable overall Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) of 24:1, well within the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 recommended benchmark of 30:1.
Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) at the Secondary stage improved to 71.7%, while the Middle stage GER stood at 89.6%.

national_news.title: Security Agencies Bust ISI-Backed Shahzad Bhatti Network in Multi-State Operation
bullets: Security agencies detained 253 people across 14 states on August 12 in a major crackdown against the ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN).
Over 80 FIRs and 200+ arrests have been recorded against SBN under provisions including UAPA, BNS, and the Arms Act.
Recoveries from the syndicate included IEDs, Pakistan Ordnance Factory-marked grenades, and espionage equipment.

national_news.title: Department of Financial Services Hosts PSB Confluence 2026
bullets: The Department of Financial Services (DFS) organized the PSB Confluence 2026 focusing on themes like Deposit Mobilisation, Banking for Youth, and Investment Cycles.
Union Finance Minister announced that a High-powered Committee on Banking Reforms for Viksit Bharat will be established soon.
Noted that historically low Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) provide Public Sector Banks with a strong foundation for the next phase of reforms.

national_news.title: India Leads Global Areca Nut Production
bullets: India is the world's largest producer of areca nut (betel nut), accounting for approximately 63% of total global production in 2025-26 according to the Directorate of Arecanut and Spices Development (DASD).
Total arecanut cultivation area reached 11.06 lakh hectares with a production of 15.29 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, up from 14.91 lakh tonnes in the previous year.
Karnataka is the largest producing state in India, yielding about 10 lakh tonnes, followed by Kerala, Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, West Bengal, and Tamil Nadu.

national_news.title: Centre Approves Qadian-Beas Railway Line Project in Punjab
bullets: The Centre approved a detailed estimate of ₹1,419.05 crore for the 39.68 km Qadian-Beas broad gauge railway line in Punjab's Majha region.
The project will be executed by Northern Railway and includes infrastructure like two crossing stations (Ghuman and Butala), 11 major bridges, 121 minor bridges, and 54 Road Under Bridges (RUBs).
The corridor will also feature the deployment of Kavach, India's indigenous train collision avoidance system, and serves as an alternative strategic route for the Amritsar–Pathankot section.

national_news.title: India-EU Trade Pact and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism Challenges
bullets: India and the European Union concluded negotiations for a major Free Trade Agreement (FTA) in January 2026.
The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its definitive financial phase concurrently, posing potential policy friction.
Differences in carbon cost measurement and recognition between Indian domestic regulations and EU's CBAM risk imposing a double compliance burden on Indian exporters, threatening FTA gains.

bihar_news.title: Hoymiles Commissions 7.7 MW Solar Project in Gaya, Bihar Under PM-KUSUM
bullets: Global energy solutions company Hoymiles commissioned a 7.7 MW solar power project in Gaya, Bihar, marking its first project under the PM-KUSUM initiative.
The project utilizes 20 units of HINV350HX-G2 string inverters, each with a rated capacity of 350 kW, executed by Naw Dharam Energy as the EPC partner.
The HINV350HX-G2 inverter features six maximum power point trackers (MPPTs), IP66 protection, C5 anti-corrosion capability, and a maximum efficiency of 99.05%.

bihar_news.title: Bihar to Resume Mining Activities After October 15, Announces CM Samrat Choudhary
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced that the state is expected to resume mining activities after October 15, following progress in the auction of critical mineral blocks.
The tender process for 28 mining blocks is underway, with over 30 blocks targeted for allotment before the end of September.
The state government has also set a target to attract Rs 5 lakh crore in investment by November and create one crore jobs by 2030.

bihar_news.title: Ministry of Mines Organises Roadshow for 8th Tranche of Critical Mineral Blocks in Patna
bullets: The Ministry of Mines organized a roadshow in Patna for the 8th Tranche of Auction of Critical and Strategic Mineral Blocks along with a workshop on the National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust (NMEDT).
The event was chaired by Union Minister of State for Coal and Mines Satish Chandra Dubey, alongside Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and State Mines Minister Pramod Kumar.
The 8th tranche comprises 20 mineral blocks—including 3 Mining Lease and 17 Composite Licence blocks—covering minerals like Graphite, Rare Earth Elements (REE), Vanadium, and Potash.

bihar_news.title: Overview of Bihar's Administrative Structure and District Demographics
bullets: Bihar comprises 38 districts administered under 9 administrative divisions: Patna, Tirhut, Saran, Darbhanga, Kosi, Purnia, Bhagalpur, Munger, and Magadh.
West Champaran is the largest district by area (5,229 sq km), while Sheohar is the smallest; Patna is the most populous district.
Bihar shares its international border with Nepal to the north (touched by 7 districts) and state borders with Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Sets Rs 5 Lakh Crore Investment Target and Announces Policy Reforms
bullets: Bihar announced an ambitious investment target of Rs 5 lakh crore by November.
New industrial policies and educational initiatives were highlighted to boost economic growth in the state.
The government aims to provide jobs for 1 crore youths by the year 2030.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Plans New Airports and Helipads to Boost Regional Connectivity and Tourism
bullets: Bihar government has formulated plans to develop new airports and helipads across the state to enhance air connectivity, tourism, and investment.
The initiative involves close coordination with the Union Civil Aviation Ministry and other relevant authorities.
Aimed at strengthening the transport infrastructure to drive economic growth and attract industrial investments in Bihar.

bihar_news.title: Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Bihar Led to Record Voter Turnout in Assembly Polls: CEC
bullets: Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar stated that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar significantly boosted voter turnout.
The 2025 Bihar assembly polls registered a record voter turnout of 67.25 per cent, the highest since Independence.
Around 70 lakh names were removed during the three-month revision exercise, which the Election Commission successfully executed for the first time in the state.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government to Build 100 Modern Bus Stands to Strengthen Transport Infrastructure
bullets: Bihar government announced plans to construct 100 new, modern bus stands equipped with advanced facilities across the state.
The announcement was made during the unveiling of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's statue in Jamui district.
The initiative is designed to ramp up road transport connectivity, improve urban infrastructure, and accelerate industrial development.

bihar_news.title: Railway Ministry Approves Sherghati-Kajree Broad Gauge Rail Link Connecting Bihar and Jharkhand
bullets: The Railway Ministry issued a sanction memorandum for the 107.89-km Sherghati-Kajree broad gauge railway line.
The project has an estimated cost of ₹2,627.29 crore, connecting Sherghati in Bihar's Gaya district with Kajree in Jharkhand's Palamu district.
The project is executed by the East Central Railway and is expected to reduce travel distance by 70 km while boosting trade and employment.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Government Warns Doctors Against Unnecessary Patient Referrals
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary issued a strict warning to government doctors against unnecessary patient referrals during a public event in Jamui.
The state government is equipping district and sub-divisional hospitals to perform 36 types of surgeries locally to reduce patient movement.
The event also witnessed the unveiling of a statue of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel in Jhajha, alongside participation from key state ministers.
